Recharging After Busy Social Times

For anyone who enjoys people but feels drained after a full day of them. Each day is one small way to plan, protect and enjoy quiet time to recover after gatherings, workdays, trips and holidays, without feeling guilty for needing it.

Rest · Self-Care · Social Anxiety · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Pick one evening this month and write "quiet night" on your calendar in pencil.
  • Day 2Take one slow breath before you open your next message today, and let your shoulders soften as you breathe out.
  • Day 3Dim the lights in your living room an hour before bed tonight, and notice how the evening slows.
  • Day 4Tell someone close to you, in a kind and simple way, that you would love a quiet hour tonight.
  • Day 5Notice one small, easy moment with someone today, like a friendly hello, and let yourself enjoy remembering it.
  • Day 6Leave a free hour after the next plan on your calendar, so you can wind down at your own pace.
  • Day 7Step outside for a minute of fresh air during your next gathering, then head back in when you are ready.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Name three things in your home that make it feel restful, and appreciate them as you pass by.
  • Day 60Remember that enjoying people and needing time alone can both be true about you at once.
  • Day 120Glance at the social plans you have coming up, and ask whether the amount feels right for you.
  • Day 240Consider how your idea of a good evening has changed over the years, and honor what you enjoy now.
  • Day 365End the day by saying to yourself, "I enjoyed people today, and now I get to rest."

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
